messages:
alex: quick sync — want to align on the long-term routing + isolation roadmap we present at leadership. core ask: what do we actually commit to for Q3-Q4 next year?
maya: +1. customers keep asking for stronger isolation and predictable SLAs across geos. need clear launch criteria.
sam: can we be explicit about which levers we promise? e.g., region pinning, per-tenant capacity reservations, hard fallbacks to lower-cost variants. customers expect contracts for latency percentiles.
paul: agree. propose we break roadmap into three deliverables: 1) policy backplane (declarative routing + tiering), 2) regional resilience primitives (drain/evacuate, per-region quotas), 3) tenant isolation modes (soft, hard, dedicated). each with clear acceptance tests.
liz: +1 to the decomposition. also we should call out econometrics: how much unit-cost delta between soft vs hard isolation? PMs need numbers to sell Dedicated.
alex: thinking we present a gated rollout: pilot with a handful of enterprise customers (canary), then general availability for Dedicated contracts. launch criteria per deliverable.
maya: rough acceptance tests idea: policy backplane = 99% correctness on routing rules for synthetic traffic; regional resilience = <1% request loss during simulated region outage; tenant isolation = no cross-tenant KV cache leaks in fuzz tests.
sam: add quality regression: run full eval suite on model variants when fallbacks happen — ensure top-3 prompts don't regress beyond threshold.
infra-bot: deploy-check: canary infra test harness triggered for project routing-backplane at 2026-03-15T09:00Z. status: scheduled.
paul: tradeoffs: soft isolation (namespaces + CPU/GPU cgroups) is fast and cheap but weaker guarantees. hard isolation (dedicated pools) is costly but needed for regulated customers. need pricing tiers mapped to these modes.
liz: customer asks summary from sales: 1) geo-residency enforcement, 2) SLA-backed latency for inference, 3) deterministic failover paths. they want concrete SLOs before committing.
alex: OK so action items for product doc: - define policy DSL primitives (weight, affinity, fallback, region) - define resilience exercises and pass/fail signals - list 3 example customer flows and acceptance SLOs.
maya: for the policy DSL draft, here's tiny example for discussion:
```
route: 
  name: european-strict
  match: region == eu-west-1 && model.version == v2
  actions:
    - prefer: dedicated-pool-eu
    - fallback: regional-shared-eu (max-latency-ms: 300)
    - quarantine: true
```
sam: that's helpful. also include capacity hedging rules: when dedicated pool < 20% available, spill to regional-shared with throttling and degrade-quality header.
paul: propose we add launch gating metrics to tickets: cost-per-100k tokens delta estimated, latency P95 target, isolation breach = zero occurrences in 30d canary.
liz: let's also include a customer communication cadence for onramp: README + runbook + post-cutover validation window (48h). sales wants a standard checklist.
alex: timeline proposal: Q2 — policy backplane MVP + pilot; Q3 — regional resilience primitives; Q4 — tenant isolation modes + GA for Dedicated. adjustable if pilot shows regressions.
maya: prioritization guidance: prioritize features that unblock 3 named enterprise deals or reduce token cost by >10% for platform customers.
sam: small note on telemetry: we need per-route token-level cost and per-tenant tail-latency heatmaps before GA. that's non-negotiable.
paul: ok owners? alex -> product lead, maya -> architecture design + DSL, sam -> telemetry + canary tests, liz -> customer onramp docs. infra-bot will track tasks.
infra-bot: created epic: longterm-routing-isolation (owner: alex) — backlog items assigned.
alex: perfect. I'll draft the product brief with the decomposed deliverables and acceptance tests and share by end of week. any objections?
maya: none from me.
sam: good to go.
liz: no objections.
paul: fine.
alex: closing thread — will push PR to /docs/roadmaps this afternoon and tag the sales/eng leads. :rocket:
